bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent drives 32.7% monthly gain; Muse ecosystem partnerships expand
bullets.body: META gained ~32.7% this month (best month since 2013) on Muse AI agent momentum. EXPE, CART, SHOP, and PayPal announced Muse integrations; prior OAI DevDay partnerships faded 2-8% from intraday highs (CART -4.2%, EXPE -7.1%). META Connect keynote tonight at 7pm EST; 'Watermelon' release pushed to early October. GS consumer inertia basket (GSXUSWCH) down 2.6% as agentic AI disruption trade intensifies.

bullets.title: EXPE/BKNG/ABNB: Muse partnership creates prisoners' dilemma for OTAs
bullets.body: EXPE became first major OTA to partner with Meta Muse for trip planning and booking; shares reversed from initial pressure on disintermediation risk. BKNG and ABNB face pressure to follow suit or risk losing traffic; ABNB most exposed (~90% direct traffic could face higher CAC). OTA performance marketing spend ~$15B this year; agentic channels could structurally alter the travel funnel targeting ~$1T offline travel spend.

bullets.title: CART: Muse integration positive but margin vulnerability flagged
bullets.body: CART announced Muse partnership converting natural language prompts into shoppable grocery carts; stock +3.6% pre-market. CART trades at ~6x '28E EBITDA; Muse provides growth/share-gain optionality vs WMT/AMZN disruption risk. Analyst note flags CART EBITDA vulnerable to deterioration given ad revenue concentration—longest downside among sector peers.

bullets.title: MU: Citi raises PT to $1,300; Wolfe bullish on DRAM/HBM; Burry shorts
bullets.body: Citi raises MU target to $1,300 (from $1,150) on better-than-expected non-LTA DRAM pricing. Wolfe forecasts strong DRAM/HBM pricing into CY28; MU trades at 6.9x FY27E EPS vs 10x thru-cycle (PT $1,500 Outperform); expects MU/SKHY FCF to fund 25-32% market-cap buybacks in CY26-27. MU earnings expected Sept 30 at consensus $31.45 EPS/$50.85B revenue. Contrarily, Michael Burry disclosed increased short positions in MU.

bullets.title: MSFT: Stifel upgrades to Buy, $575 PT; Copilot discounts to drive adoption
bullets.body: Stifel upgrades MSFT to Buy from Hold, raises PT to $575 (from $530) citing sustainable mid-to-upper-teens revenue growth via LLM-agnostic Azure strategy. MSFT offering 30-50% Copilot discounts for large corporate commitments and launching AI 'Super App'; ServiceNow on track to exceed $1.5B CY26 AI ACV with SKU-upgrade monetization.

bullets.title: NVDA: Insider sells $300M; forward P/E at decade-low 15.75x; IONQ partnership
bullets.body: NVDA board member Mark Stevens sold ~$300M in shares. NVDA forward P/E hit 15.75x, lowest in over a decade. IonQ's Superion 256 QPU will be first at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center (NVAQC), integrating with GB200 NVL72 via NVQLink/CUDA-Q. AVGO expects 100% supply-constrained YoY growth; NVDA expects 70% supply-constrained growth next year.

bullets.title: IONQ: +11.8% pre-market on real-time quantum error decoder and NVDA partnership
bullets.body: IONQ surged 11.8% pre-market on demonstration of end-to-end real-time quantum error decoder, with QBTS and RGTI moving sympathetically. IONQ's Superion 256 QPU to be installed at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center, integrating with GB200 NVL72 for hybrid quantum-GPU co-design.

bullets.title: MRVL: Seaport initiates Buy at $270; UBS initiates CRWV Buy at $120
bullets.body: Seaport Research Partners initiates MRVL at Buy with $270 PT (3% upside), alongside ON Buy at $100 (36% upside). UBS initiates CRWV at Buy with $120 PT. Taiwan August export orders surged 71.4% YoY to record $103B on AI/custom ASIC demand.

bullets.title: NET: Citi $400 PT; Cloudflare consumption accelerating as pool-of-funds exhausted
bullets.body: Citi prefers NET over Fastly (FSLY); NET trades at ~0.8x EV/S/G on 33% CY26-29E CAGR with $400 PT; positioned as AI-inference winner with deeper enterprise GTM. JPM software checks show Cloudflare consumption driving revenue acceleration as customers exhaust pool-of-funds commitments early; Act IV monetization still in development. NET hit 52-week high today.

bullets.title: SPOT: Down 3% on Q4 gross margin concerns; AI disruption risk seen as overstated
bullets.body: SPOT fell ~3% after management nudged Q4 gross margin guidance below Street consensus (33.9%), citing AI token costs. JPM view: agentic AI disruption concerns overstated given no discount model and subscriber stickiness to AVOD tier, though SPOT remains on the 'JPM Agentic Vulnerable Index.'

bullets.title: SNOW: AI contributed ~50% of F2Q beat; growing core migration opportunity
bullets.body: Snowflake's AI workloads contributed roughly 50% of its F2Q beat and are becoming a more meaningful growth driver. The core Global 2000 migration opportunity remains substantial—average spend $2.4M vs $34M for top 25 customers.

bullets.title: NBIS: Up to 20% price hikes on H200/H100; B300 at highest on-demand pricing
bullets.body: NBIS implementing price hikes up to 20% on H200 and H100 GPU instances; B300 on-demand pricing at highest levels seen from any vendor. Stock previously rallied $20+ following prior price hike announcements. Michael Burry also disclosed increased short positions in NBIS.

bullets.title: PLTR/MU/NBIS: Michael Burry increases short positions across AI/semi names
bullets.body: Michael Burry disclosed increased short positions in Micron (MU), Nebius (NBIS), and Palantir (PLTR) in latest filing. Bearish on semiconductors broadly.

bullets.title: HUBS: FBN initiates Sector Perform at $230 PT; JPM webinar on agentic trial adoption
bullets.body: FBN Securities initiates HubSpot at Sector Perform with $230 PT (6% upside from $217.88). JPM software checks show HubSpot agentic trial adoption broadened from ~37% to >55% of customers; AI connector users show ~12pt higher retention.

bullets.title: AMZN: Trading at AWS + Anthropic value with zero credit for other assets; Bearish Hedgeye signal
bullets.body: AMZN described as 'trading at AWS + Anthropic stake value with zero value assigned to other segments'; AWS positioned to gain pricing leverage from VM infrastructure demand. Hedgeye maintains Bearish trend on AMZN (buy level $244, sell $260). BBY-AMZN Fire TV partnership expands to include programmatic advertising integration starting Feb 2027.

bullets.title: DELL: MS bullish on agentic AI TAM expansion; supply constraints could last 5+ years
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlights DELL bull case as likely to play out; agentic AI to drive 87x inference token growth by 2030, requiring greater compute/storage. DELL sees infra margins improving with floor shifting higher; component supply shortages (DRAM, optical, PCB) flagged as biggest constraint potentially lasting 5+ years.

bullets.title: HOOD: Hedgeye initiates slight long; Active Trader Summit Sept 29-30
bullets.body: Hedgeye starts HOOD with slight long bias, noting ~50% of revenue remains high-margin 'degenerate trading' but current multiple assumes good times continue. MS upgrades HOOD on agentic trading summit thesis; Active Trader Summit Sept 29-30 expected to feature agentic trading and U.S. perpetual futures as product focus.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro demand strong; TSMC 2nm chips shipping; 52-week high today
bullets.body: Taiwan telcos report 60-70% YoY surge in iPhone 18 Pro pre-sales in first 3 days (Chunghwa +60%, Far Eastone +70%). TSMC 2nm chips confirmed shipping in iPhone 18 Pro series. AAPL hit new all-time high with market cap exceeding $5T. Hedgeye maintains Bullish trend (buy level $327, sell $345).

bullets.title: TSLA: Hedgeye upgrades to Bullish trend; buy level $360
bullets.body: Hedgeye changed TSLA from Neutral to Bullish trend with buy level $360, sell $382. Tesla Bot deployment in Tesla vehicles expected by fall 2026 alongside Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 releases.

bullets.title: CHTR/CMCSA/T/VZ: Starlink capacity capped at ~10% US penetration by 2030
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley conversation with Recon Analytics finds Starlink max US penetration at 10-12M subs by 2030 (vs 16M consensus) due to dense-area capacity constraints. Cable sub losses to continue despite improving NPS; Charter has largest global Wi-Fi 7 deployment. T-Mobile fastest growing operator, on track to be most profitable.
